entries.subject: DAMIT 548: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-548.txt. Model 548, version 2013-02-11, pole (141°, -11°), period 6.58167 h match the retained metadata. The archive supplies no diameter for this model; a separate scale constraint is required. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: AKARI AcuA
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — included as an explicitly approximate thermal size transfer. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 37.89 ± 0.65 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 193 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 549, pole ['328', '-17'], [Model 549](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/549) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 549: pole (328°, -17°), 6.58167 h, version 2013-02-11. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.

entries.subject: PDS SBN catalogue values that disagree with the factsheet or are not shown
entries.finding: The display scale "18.945 km (approximate thermal scale)" (akari-acua-v1) implies a diameter of 37.89 km, outside the added Small Bodies Occultations V4.0 record 140, DAMIT model 548 diameter 34 ± 1 km (volume-equivalent; DAMIT model 548 fitted to 1 occultation). Both are shown; the display scale is not changed.
entries.revisitWhen: A newer release of the named catalogue, or a review that replaces the shown value.
